reasoning: A hybrid approach combines autonomous reasoning to identify common feature patterns across misclassified instances with external XAI tools to quantitatively measure feature attribution and detect spurious correlations. This ensures both intuitive pattern recognition and statistically grounded importance scores, improving accuracy in identifying shared spurious features that are not semantically linked to the target label.

autonomous_tasks.query: Compare the feature values across instances 13590, 2021, and 12840 to identify which features appear in all three and are not directly semantically related to income prediction.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of features that are common to all three misclassified instances and may be spurious

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any common feature (e.g., marital-status=Married-civ-spouse, education=HS-grad) is semantically tied to income class or whether it might be a spurious correlation due to co-occurrence with other factors.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A judgment on whether the shared features are semantically relevant or spurious

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides global feature importance with intersection analysis to confirm shared influence across misclassified instances. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local interpretability to validate attribution strength, while sensitivity analysis measures the impact of removing features to detect spurious dependencies. Together, they validate whether shared features are causally or spuriously influential in misclassification.
